title: 😂 Face with Tears of Joy Emoji Meaning and Gen Z Verdict
description: The face with tears of joy emoji 😂 means laughing so hard you cry. Long the world's favorite emoji, it now divides generations. See who uses it and what replaced it.
summary: The 😂 face with tears of joy means something is so funny the sender is crying with laughter. It is the standard laughing emoji and one of the most used emojis ever. Many younger people now consider it dated and use 💀 or 😭 instead, but its meaning is unchanged.
meaning: No emoji has had a bigger career. 😂 became the default way to say “that's hilarious” in the early smartphone years, and in 2015 Oxford Dictionaries chose it as its Word of the Year, the first time a pictograph received the title. The expression is easy to read: eyes crinkled shut, mouth wide, a tear at each corner. It says you laughed until your eyes watered.

In daily use it covers a wide range, from real laughter to a simple acknowledgment that something was meant as a joke. Plenty of people add 😂 to the end of their own sentences as a tone marker, the way they might say “lol.” In that role it does not claim tears; it tells the reader not to take the line too seriously.

Around the start of the 2020s, younger users on TikTok began calling 😂 a millennial habit and moved to the skull and the loud crying face for laughter. The shift is real but partial. 😂 remains extremely common worldwide, and millions of people of every age still use it without a second thought. Whether it looks dated depends on who is reading.

Like all laughing emojis, it can cut. A lone 😂 in reply to a heartfelt message, an opinion, or a mistake suggests the reader finds the person ridiculous. In arguments online it is a common way to dismiss someone without engaging. The face is the same; the target is what changes.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: The all-purpose response to anything funny, and a softener for teasing: “you're such a nerd 😂” is affectionate where the bare sentence might sting. The number sent tends to scale with the laugh. One is polite amusement, three or more is real laughter, and a full row is helplessness.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Still everywhere in comments, though heavy Gen Z spaces favor 💀 and 😭. Some younger users deploy 😂 ironically to imitate an older relative or a brand account. On Instagram it remains one of the default quick reactions to stories, so it is sent constantly regardless of fashion.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Acceptable in casual chat with colleagues, particularly as a reaction to a joke. It is too informal for clients or senior leaders you do not know. Take care not to use it in threads about problems, where it may seem to make light of someone's error.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: Its meaning travels well, since crying with laughter is understood nearly everywhere. Usage rates differ by country and platform, and in many places it never fell from favor at all. Where WhatsApp is the main messaging app, 😂 and 🤣 dominate family and community groups.

Sharing a meme that matches the friendship.

combos.meaning: Proper, sustained laughter; the more repeats, the funnier it was.
So funny it “killed” them; bridges the old and new laugh emojis.
Laughing and applauding a joke, roast, or perfect reply.
That was funny and I adore you; common between partners and family.

confusedWith.difference: 😭 shows continuous streams of tears and an open wail. It officially means sobbing, and younger users also use it for laughter and for anything overwhelming. 😂 has small tears and a grin, and is only ever laughter.
🤣 is tilted on its side with bigger tears and a wider mouth, showing someone who has toppled over laughing. It is the more intense of the two. 😂 sits upright and is the everyday choice.
🥲 has a gentle closed smile and one tear on the cheek. It means bittersweet feelings or smiling through sadness. It has nothing to do with laughing, though the tear makes people mix them up.

avoid: Don't send it in response to someone's sincere feelings, bad news, or a serious question.
Avoid ending every sentence with it, which can make messages hard to read and your tone hard to judge.
Hold off in formal or first-contact professional messages, where it is too casual.
design: A yellow face with tightly closed, upward-curving eyes, a broad open grin showing the upper teeth, and one light-blue tear at the outer corner of each eye. Raised eyebrows appear on several platforms. Apple, Google, Samsung, Microsoft, and WhatsApp all draw the same concept, differing in tear size and how far the face seems to lean back.

faqs.a: Among some teens and young adults, yes; they tend to use 💀 or 😭 for laughter and may see 😂 as something their parents send. Across all users it is still one of the most popular emojis, and using it will not confuse anyone.

faqs.q: What does 😂 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: They think something is funny. If they send it often in reply to you, they enjoy your humor, which is a good sign in friendship and dating alike. It does not carry romantic meaning the way hearts or winks do.

Laughing. The tears are from laughing too hard, and the wide smile confirms it. For sadness people use 😢 or 😭. If someone replies 😂 to sad news, they have probably misread the message or picked the wrong face.

faqs.q: Why was 😂 named Word of the Year?
faqs.a: Oxford Dictionaries picked it for 2015 because it judged that the emoji best captured the mood and habits of that year, when emoji use had surged and 😂 was the most widely used of all.

faqs.q: What can I use instead of 😂?
faqs.a: For a similar meaning try 🤣 for a bigger laugh or 😆 for a lighter one. To match younger usage, 💀 means “I'm dead” from laughing and 😭 means crying with laughter. Typing “lol” or “haha” also still works.
